caption:
The truth about hyaluronic acid fillers 🧬

Recently, hyaluronic acid (HA) fillers have received some negative attention — but it’s important to understand that when performed correctly, fillers remain one of the safest and most effective treatments for facial rejuvenation.

HA fillers are designed to restore lost volume, smooth fine lines and wrinkles, and enhance facial structure — such as defining the jawline or addressing a receding chin. The results and safety of the procedure depend largely
transcript: Hi everyone, uh Dr. Ariel Lostat here. I wanted to uh talk to you about a very important topic that tends to come up a lot in the exam room and that is the use of hyaluronic acid fillers. I find a lot of patients have maybe noted on their friends or on social media people who may be overfilled and therefore they're not looking natural. And uh it is something that we tend to see as a trend. It is not an issue with the use of hyaluronic acid. It unfortunately has a lot to do with the technique that's used in terms of which product, how it's injected, where it's injected, and really the artistry of creating amazing results in a subtle manner. So, so much of it is technique dependent and the amount of filler that's put in. I find that in my practice, uh, I am proud to say I really understand the facial features, proportions. So we can really address these issues by using the correct fillers uh that are placed in the right place that does not lead to rounding of the face and overfilling of the face. Having said that, there's also some newer techniques that one can use for people who may not be interested in using hyaluronic acid fillers and that is using the regenerative powers of your own blood. Uh what I've been doing a lot in the last year is basically doing a procedure called PRFM which stands for plateletri fibbrin matrix. It's utilizing one's own blood. We draw the patient's blood. We spin it in a centriuge which separates. We take we discard the red component which has the red blood cells and then we take the clear component which is plasma which is packed with growth factors. There are basically molecules like vascular endothelial growth factor, fibiberblast growth factor, platelet drive growth factor. These all induce collagen formation, elastin formation. They do induce neoangioenesis which is increased blood flow. Therefore, the skin looks healthier. But one thing I do is we actually add thromben to it. Thromben causes the PRP to become slightly coagulated and therefore turns into a gel and as a result it can be used as a bio stimulator or as a filler. I've used it very commonly on lower eyelids, laugh lines, forehead wrinkles and it does definitely stimulate collagen. It can act as a filler. It won't work as well as a filler in terms of immediate effects, but it does definitely slowly induce collagen formation over time. It's a procedure that does need to be repeated typically about three times done once a month. But my patients are very happy with …[truncated]

transcript: If you're about to spend thousands of dollars on a laser treatment, stop. And these are four mistakes that I absolutely want you to avoid, especially the last one. If you are prone to hyperpigmentation. Before you touch your face. I'm Doctor Edris, and this is what I would want you to know before you spend thousands of dollars touching your face. When you ask, what are we treating? And the answer you get is the name of the laser, I would probably run, cause that's not the answer you're looking for. And if someone can't explain to you what they're treating and how in plain English, I wouldn't let them treat my face. Because ultimately you have to diagnose the problem first in order to understand how a machine is going to fix it. If someone tells you you need six sessions before they've ever even treated you, I would pause, because how the hell do you know that you even need six sessions yet? And unless we're talking about something like laser hair removal, where we know we're gonna need multiple sessions, I personally would much rather treat you, see how you respond, and then decide how you wanna proceed. Now here is where I would be careful. If somebody tells you that their laser can target your wrinkles, your redness, your pigmentation, and even tighten your skin, I'd be skeptical. There is no single laser that is best for everything. And honestly, I trust somebody more when They tell me what a laser can't do. And this one I really want you to hear. Especially if you tend to pigment, because the wrong laser can leave you with way more pigment than what you walked in with. Are you prepping your skin? And ask your provider. Are you being conservative with my settings? Because you should be okay to get more treatments at a more conservative setting than try to get one treatment that might blast your face off.
